newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra to make competition payments to states.
newsitem.headline: Canberra to make competition payments to states.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday all states and territories would receive federal government payments for implementing specific competition reforms in their own jurisdictions.
Costello said the decision to make the payments was based on recommendations from the National Competition Council.
"The council has recommended that all states and territories should receive their payments in 1997/98," Costello said in a statement.
"This is in recognition of the progress that individual jurisdictions have made in implementing the necessary reforms."
He said the council had also reached agreements with some states and territories in relation to the unsatisfactory implementation of particular reforms.
The council also recommended a review of the reform process in each state or territory before payments were made in 1998/99.

"The most important of these reforms are the national gas reforms, the progression of the legislation review requirements in relation to various pieces of gaming legislation, and the application of the principles of the Competition Principles Agreement," Costello said.
The payments related to an agreement made at the April 1995 Council of Australian Governments meeting and would total A$406 million in 1997/98, he said.
